name: Lethal Brain and Heart Developmental Defects
aliases: Severe Congenital Brain and Cardiac Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of severe structural brain malformations such as holoprosencephaly or agenesis of the corpus callosum
Identification of critical congenital heart defects including hypoplastic left heart syndrome or complex septal defects
Detection of pathogenic variants in genes known to affect brain and heart development

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least one major brain malformation and one major cardiac defect confirmed by imaging or pathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and prenatal imaging are critical for early diagnosis and counseling.

pathognomonic.notes: Failure of forebrain division leading to severe brain malformation
Underdevelopment of left-sided heart structures causing critical cardiac failure
searchTerms: small left side of heart at birth

pathognomonic.notes: Complete or partial absence of the corpus callosum

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to neurological impairment
searchTerms: difficulty feeding due to nerve problems
trouble swallowing related to brain dysfunction
delayed development starting before or at birth
slow growth and milestones from prenatal causes

occasional.notes: Epileptic episodes secondary to brain malformations

searchTerms: cyanosis due to poor heart function

occasional.notes: Accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid causing increased intracranial pressure
Secondary to cardiac failure or neurological impairment
Reduced muscle tone due to central nervous system involvement

rare.notes: Absence of one or both kidneys
Extra digits on hands or feet

laboratory: Elevated brain-specific proteins in cerebrospinal fluid
Abnormal cardiac enzyme levels in neonates
imaging: Echocardiography revealing complex congenital heart defects
MRI demonstrating agenesis of corpus callosum or holoprosencephaly
other: Prenatal detection via fetal MRI and echocardiography
Postmortem pathological confirmation of brain and heart defects

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated brain malformations without critical cardiac defects
Cardiac defects without associated severe brain malformations

redFlags: Severe prenatal ventriculomegaly or brain structural abnormalities on ultrasound
Critical cyanotic congenital heart disease detected at birth
Failure to thrive with neurological deterioration in neonate
